title: “Would you like to cook an insect-based muffin at home?” – Exploring the association between food preparation, attitudes towards entomophagy and sensory liking
abstract: Purpose This study explored how preparing insect-based foods at home influences attitudes toward entomophagy and sensory evaluation, filling a gap, as most Western research involves tasting sessions with foods prepared by others. Design/methodology/approach A total of 172 respondents from Belgium participated in this study. Participants had previously indicated that they accepted the consumption of edible insects and voluntarily agreed to participate in either a tasting activity or a cooking and tasting activity. Participants either prepared an insect-based muffin themselves or received a ready-to-eat muffin prepared by a third party. Findings No significant changes in attitudes were observed following either activity, although the high baseline acceptance limited the potential for further improvement. Nonetheless, those who prepared the insect-based muffin rated it higher on most sensory attributes compared to non-preparers. This finding is consistent with the previously described “I cooked it myself” effect, although the present study cannot establish that cooking itself caused the observed difference. Further research using direct measures of potential psychological mechanisms is therefore needed. Originality/value This study provides exploratory evidence on the association between personal preparation of an insect-based food and sensory evaluation in a home-based setting. It extends previous research on self-preparation and food appreciation to the context of edible insects.

title: رثاء الديار بين الأثر والذاكرة: قراءة نقدية في قصيدة "ديسان" للفطيسي في ضوء معارضتها لنونية الرندي The Lament of Abandoned Homes Between Trace and Memory: A Critical Reading of Al-Futaisi’s Poem ‘Disan’ in Light of Its Opposition to Al-Randi’s ‘Qasidat al-Nuniyya
abstract: تهدف هذه الدراسة إلى تقديم مقاربة تحليلية نقدية لقصيدة "ديسان" للشاعر محمد بن عبد القادر الفطيسي التي كتبها حوالي سنة (ت 1252ه – 1836م)، بوصفها أنموذجاً لأدب الأوبئة في الذاكرة الليبية. ومع أن الدراسة تسعى إلى لفت انتباه الباحثين إلى أهمية هذه القصيدة في التأريخ الأدبي لأدب الكوارث والأوبئة والمجاعات، إلا أن الإشكالية الرئيسة التي تتمحور حولها الدراسة تتمثل في تساؤل جوهري حول الآليات التي اعتمد عليها الفطيسي لتجسيد الكارثة، وتشخيص المكان المتمثل في الجبل لكي يكون فاعلاً دلالياًّ قادراً على تعويض الفقد البشري الجماعي، حيث حوَّل الفطيسي جبل "ديسان" من معلم جغرافي صامت إلى مستودع ذكريات حفظت قيم المجتمع الذي أباده الطاعون. وتعتمد الدراسة منهجاً وصفياً تحليلياً يفيد من أبعاد سيميائية المكان وجماليات التلقي، مع إجراء موازنة نقدية معمقة مع نونية أبي البقاء الرندي في رثاء الأندلس باعتبارها نصاً معارَضاً. وقد كشفت الدراسة استراتيجية جمالية وظفها الشاعر تقوم على الإحياء بالصور، وأنسنة الجبل، وتشكيل فردوس لغوي يعوض فردوس المجتمع المفقود، وجعل من شخصية (سالمة) في النص معادلاً موضوعياً لمنظومة القيم الأخلاقية المنهارة. كما أكدت الدراسة سيرورة النص عبر المعارضة والتخميس الشعري، وعبر التدوين التاريخي على يد (الطاهر الزاوي وأحمد الصاري) اللذين أسهما في نقل القصيدة من سياقها المحلي الضيق إلى مركز الذاكرة الوطنية الليبية.

title: When customers mistreat service robots: employee moral appraisals and managerial intervention
abstract: Purpose As service robots become embedded in frontline operations, employees increasingly witness customers directing rude or degrading behaviors toward service robots. Although robots are nonsentient technologies, such incidents can violate service interaction norms and disrupt the moral order of robot-augmented encounters. This study aims to examine how observed robot-directed customer mistreatment shapes employees’ moral appraisals, cognitive processing and service behaviors. Design/methodology/approach Across a multistudy research program, Study 1a uses a randomized experiment to test whether observing robot-directed customer mistreatment elicits vicarious moral emotions and deontic injustice perceptions and whether immediate managerial intervention modestly attenuates deontic injustice perceptions. Study 1b uses a construct-boundary experiment comparing robot-directed mistreatment, human-directed mistreatment and respectful customer interaction. Study 2 uses a 10-day experience-sampling design to examine within-person spillover from daily observed robot-directed customer mistreatment to evening cognition and next-workday service behavior. Study 3 uses a field quasi-experiment to assess a structured managerial intervention protocol. Findings Observed robot-directed customer mistreatment increases deontic injustice perceptions; in the daily study, these perceptions are associated with evening affective rumination and limited next-workday service withdrawal. A smaller constructive pathway links problem-solving pondering to proactive service behavior. Immediate managerial intervention modestly attenuates justice-based appraisal; in a nonrandomized field comparison, a formal intervention protocol is associated with modest improvements in proactive service behavior and withdrawal. Originality/value By using a nonsentient service robot as a boundary case, this research shows that witnessed mistreatment can remain normatively consequential even when victim-centered empathic concern is attenuated. The findings distinguish conduct-centered deontic appraisal from concern for a suffering victim and conceptualize managerial intervention as a potential form of normative repair in robot-augmented service systems.

title: Translating the EU Rural Vision 2040 to Mountain Regions: Obstacles, Pathways, and Visions From 17 European Countries
abstract: Mountain regions across Europe face interconnected demographic, economic, governance, infrastructural, and environmental challenges that require place-based and territorially adapted development approaches. This article explores how the EU Long-Term Vision for Rural Areas can be translated into actionable recommendations for mountain regions through a Theory of Change approach. The study is based on a structured expert survey conducted within the MARGISTAR COST Action, involving 24 experts from 17 European countries each representing diverse European mountain systems. Qualitative thematic analysis and inductive content analysis were used to identify elements of desirable futures, current obstacles, and revitalization pathways under the 4 pillars of the EU Rural Vision 2040: stronger, connected, resilient, and prosperous rural areas. The results highlight that mountain revitalization depends on inclusive governance, demographic renewal, digital and transport connectivity, economic diversification, climate adaptation, sustainable land use, and capacity building. Experts identified major obstacles, including depopulation, weak governance coordination, limited infrastructure, cultural barriers, and environmental pressures. The article concludes that the effective implementation of the EU Rural Vision in mountain areas requires flexible, context-sensitive, and participatory policy approaches adapted to diverse territorial realities.

The Transnational Power of International Law in a Chaotic World
journal: Political Anthropological Research on International Social Sciences (PARISS)
abstract: Abstract The international legal framework is today under unseen pressure. The principles of sovereignty and respect for international borders are openly rejected by leaders of the most powerful nations. United Nations bodies are being boycotted, and international judges and prosecutors are targeted with sanctions designed for terrorists and criminal organisations. Are we watching the agony of the international law and justice?

title: The Swedish childhood cancer quality registry for risk-based long-term follow-up after childhood cancer: structure, content, and development over time
abstract: Abstract Background Survival after childhood cancer has increased dramatically during the last 50–60 years. Today, approximately 86% of childhood cancer patients in Sweden survive more than 5 years, and most of them reach adulthood. The intense multimodal cancer treatment is unfortunately associated with a risk of late complications during childhood or later in adult life. A registry for monitoring late complications is an important tool to support structured long-term follow-up. In Sweden this is available through the SALUB database, a part of the Swedish childhood cancer quality registry. The aim of this study is to describe the SALUB database and assess its coverage, its capacity to identify treatment-defined risk groups for late complications, and the completeness of long-term follow-up data. Methods A cohort of patients who had reached at least 19 years of age, were born before 01/07/2006, and had received or were assumed to have received systemic cancer treatment or radiotherapy was identified in the Swedish childhood cancer quality registry. Database coverage was assessed by individual-level linkage, using personal identity numbers, between the SALUB database and the diagnosis-based databases. Subpopulations were assessed to explore changes over time, identify treatment-defined risk group, and assess the completeness of follow-up data. Results The coverage was 73% (3,780/5,171) in the overall cohort and 94% (803/853) in patients born between 2002 and 2006. The number of individuals at risk for cardiotoxicity and gonadal toxicity were easily identified. A total of 1,809 patients had at least one follow-up record meeting the inclusion criteria. Data completeness varied markedly across organ systems. Conclusions The SALUB database has high coverage among younger survivors and enables identification of individuals according to treatment-defined risks of late complications. However, lower coverage in older survivors and incomplete follow-up data currently limit some of its potential applications. Continued development of the database will strengthen its role in risk-based survivorship care, health care planning, and research.

title: The American Society of Clinical Psychopharmacology Task Force Consensus Statement on Combination Psychopharmacology
Experts' and AI perspectives on the environmental sustainability of tensile membrane structures
abstract: Purpose With increasing demands for sustainable construction, there is growing interest in enhancing the environmental performance of tensile membrane structures (TMS). This study aims to investigate the environmental sustainability challenges and opportunities of TMS across their lifecycle stages by integrating expert insights and advanced AI-generated perspectives. Design/methodology/approach A qualitative methodology was employed using semi-structured interviews with 16 experienced professionals including architects, engineers, contractors, builders, environmental sustainability experts and researchers. To enhance the reliability of findings and address potential gaps, the study also utilised artificial intelligence (AI) tools (ChatGPT and DeepSeek) to compare human expert insights with AI responses. Thematic analysis was conducted to categorise the results into core environmental sustainability themes. Findings Five interrelated themes were identified: (1) material innovation and environmental sustainability, (2) structural efficiency and lightweight design, (3) construction techniques and environmental sustainability alignment, (4) life durability management and (5) accessibility, inclusivity and waste management. These themes highlight critical performance indicators such as energy use, structural behaviour, material optimisation, user experience and maintenance strategies. The integration of AI insights helped highlight both consensus and gaps in expert knowledge. Originality/value This study provides a systematic qualitative investigation of environmental sustainability in TMS from an expert-practice perspective and is among the first to compare expert insights with AI-generated assessments of environmental sustainability within the TMS domain. The research contributes to the growing field of environmentally responsive structural design by offering actionable strategies for embedding environmental sustainability assessment practices into TMS planning and implementation. The findings provide valuable guidance for architects, engineers and policymakers seeking to enhance low-carbon design decisions in membrane architecture.
